requirements.label: core
requirements.title: Required core courses (9 credits)
requirements.sourceText: Required core courses (9 credits): ATM 201 - Introduction to Climate and Climate Change 3 credits OR ATM 237 - World Climate and Atmosphere 3 credits; SUS 323 - Environmental Justice 3 credits; CME 491 - Sustainable Future through Renewable Energy 3 credits

requirements.label: electives
requirements.title: Elective courses (6 credits), one course from each of 2 different paths
requirements.sourceText: Elective courses (6 credits) Select 1 course from each of 2 different paths. Natural Sciences Path: ATM 305 - Global Atmospheric Change 3 credits; BIO 319 - Landscape Ecology Laboratory 3 credits; BIO 336 - Conservation Biology 3 credits; BIO 351 - Ecology 3 credits; BIO 385 - Plant Ecology 3 credits; BIO 386 - Ecosystem Ecology and the Global Environment 3 credits; ENS 311 - Ecosystem Ecology and the Global Environment 3 credits; GSS 313 - GIS Design and Application I 3 credits; GSS 314 - GIS Laboratory 1 credit; SUS 322 - Human Ecology 3 credits; SUS 326 - Conservation Genetics 3 credits; SUS 340 - Ecological and Social Dimensions of Disease 3 credits; SUS 343 - Age of the Anthropocene 3 credits. Engineering Path: CIV 355 - Introduction to Data Science and AI for Civil Engineering 3 credits; CIV 407 - Transportation Economics 3 credits; CIV 422 - Introduction to Coastal Engineering 3 credits; CIV 423 - Coastal Engineering Planning and Design 3 credits; CIV 424 - Stormwater Management & Design 3 credits; EST 391 - Technology Assessment 3 credits. Social Sciences and Humanities Path: COM 351 - Team Collaboration and Community Engagement 3 credits; COM 365 - Talking Science 3 credits; COM 436 - Environmental Communication 3 credits; ECO 335 - Economic Development 3 credits; ECO 373 - Economics of Environment and Natural Resources 3 credits; EGL 317 - Energy Humanities and Literature 3 credits; EGL 319 - Ecology and Evolution in American Literature 3 credits; SUS 321 - Ecology and Evolution in American Literature 3 credits; EGL 372 - Topics in Women and Literature 3 credits; GLI 320 - Global, Cultural, and Environmental Issues 3 credits; HIS 365 - Environmental History of North America 3 credits; JRN 438 - Weathercasting & Environmental Reporting 3 credits; POL 371 - Politics of Climate Change 3 credits; SOC 344 - Environmental Sociology 3 credits; SUS 307 - Environmental Economics and Management 3 credits; SUS 311 - Disasters and Society: A Global Perspective 3 credits; SUS 317 - American Environmental History 3 credits; SUS 318 - American Environmental Politics 3 credits; SUS 362 - Resilient Communities 3 credits; SUS 366 - Philosophy of the Environment (III) 3 credits; PHI 366 - Philosophy of the Environment (III) 3 credits

requirements.label: capstone
requirements.title: Capstone (3 credits)

rule.manualCheck: Confirm the internship or research project is a 487/488-type course or similar and was approved in advance by the Climate Solutions Minor Director or Steering Committee.
rule.text: Internship (488 course, or similar) or independent research with a faculty mentor (487 course, or similar), which must be approved in advance by the Climate Solutions Minor Director or Steering Committee.
rule.reason: "488 course, or similar" and "487 course, or similar" name no fixed course list, so the eligible courses cannot be enumerated.

requirements.sourceText: Capstone (3 credits): Internship (488 course, or similar) or independent research with a faculty mentor (487 course, or similar), which must be approved in advance by the Climate Solutions Minor Director or Steering Committee.

requirements.label: overlap-credits
requirements.title: Credits not shared with another major or minor

rule.text: At least 12 credits applied to the minor may not be applied to any major or other minor.
rule.reason: Cross-program credit limits cannot be checked against other programs' requirements by this rule set.

requirements.sourceText: At least 12 credits applied to the minor may not be applied to any major or other minor.

requirements.label: overlap-electives
requirements.title: Limit on shared electives

rule.text: Of the 6 credits that could be also applied to another major or minor, no more than one course can be from the electives list below.
rule.reason: Cross-program overlap limit depends on another program's requirements, which this rule set cannot evaluate.
